message.abstract: <jats:p>Given a separably closed field <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline1"/><jats:tex-math>$K$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> of characteristic <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline2"/><jats:tex-math>$p>0$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> and finite degree of imperfection, we study the <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline3"/><jats:tex-math>$\sharp$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> functor which takes a semiabelian variety <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline4"/><jats:tex-math>$G$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> over <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline5"/><jats:tex-math>$K$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> to the maximal divisible subgroup of <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline6"/><jats:tex-math>$G(K)$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. Our main result is an example where <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline7"/><jats:tex-math>$G^{\sharp }$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, as a ‘type-definable group’ in <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline8"/><jats:tex-math>$K$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, does not have ‘relative Morley rank’, yielding a counterexample to a claim in Hrushovski [<jats:italic>J. Amer. Math. Soc.</jats:italic> <jats:bold>9</jats:bold> (1996), 667–690]. Our methods involve studying the question of the preservation of exact sequences by the <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline9"/><jats:tex-math>$\sharp$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> functor, and relating this to issues of descent as well as model-theoretic properties of <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline10"/><jats:tex-math>$G^{\sharp }$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. We mention some characteristic 0 analogues of these ‘exactness-descent’ results, where differential algebraic methods are more prominent. We also develop the notion of an iterative D-structure on a group scheme over an iterative Hasse field, which is interesting in its own right, as well as providing a uniform treatment of the characteristic 0 and characteristic <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S147474801400022X_inline11"/><jats:tex-math>$p$</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> cases of ‘exactness descent’.</jats:p>
